title: Release bump misses .claude-plugin/plugin.json: 0.4.3 marketplace pin resolves as 0.4.2
description: Found by opum-agent when the marketplace pin moved to v0.4.3: claude plugin update opum-lore reported already at the latest version (0.4.2). Verified: package.json at tag v0.4.3 is 0.4.3, but .claude-plugin/plugin.json at the same tag is still 0.4.2 -- LCLI-445's release cut bumped all 7 npm package manifests but never touched the plugin manifest. Claude Code's plugin-update resolution reads plugin.json's own version, so a pinned tag whose plugin.json did not move is invisible to every installed copy of the opum-lore plugin: a fresh install of v0.4.3's tree still labels itself 0.4.2. This is the same failure class opum-marketplace's own version guard exists to catch (OPAG-32), reproduced here because nothing on the lore-cli side checks it. Not urgent: the plugin's skill content is byte-identical between 0.4.2 and 0.4.3 (LCLI-443/444 touched only the CLI and this repo's own config, not the plugin skill), so no installed copy is running stale instructions -- but fix the process, not just this one tag by hand. Ship the fix in 0.4.4 whenever that release happens; no need to cut a release for this alone.

acceptanceCriteria.text: docs/runbooks/release-publishing.md Step 3 (or wherever the version-bump checklist lives) explicitly bumps .claude-plugin/plugin.json to the same version as package.json, in the same commit as the other 7 manifests
a test or CI step fails when .claude-plugin/plugin.json and package.json versions disagree, so this cannot silently recur
the next real release (0.4.4 or later) carries a plugin.json matching its own package.json version, verified directly at the tag

implementationNotes: Runbook updated (docs/runbooks/release-publishing.md Step 3, item 2): bumping .claude-plugin/plugin.json alongside the other 7 manifests is now an explicit checklist step. New test/plugin-manifest.test.ts (AC#2) asserts plugin.json.version === package.json.version, part of the normal bun test run so it fails on every PR the moment the two disagree, not only at release-dispatch time. dev's plugin.json bumped to 0.4.3 to match the currently-released package.json (fixing the drift left by 0.4.3's own cut). AC#3 (verified at the next real release) stays open until 0.4.4 or later actually ships -- will check it off then.
